messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: P0: continuous-batching latency spike in us-west-2. 95th pct token latency > 6s, error-rate up. Automatic paging to oncall.
maria (oncall): acked. I'm pulling dashboards now — tagging alex and sophia for runtime context.
alex (sre): seeing a huge KV cache eviction rate spike correlated with throughput burst. KV cache size went from 4GB -> 0.6GB in ~30s and then evictions kept rising.
sophia (eng-runtime): that eviction storm would blow CPU waiting on fetches, causing microbatch queue pileup. any recent rollout? deploy-bot: deploy 1787 released 6m ago to cb-controller on us-west-2.
ryan (product): any customer impact? alerts showing increased 502s on streaming endpoints for some customers.
maria (oncall): quick customer triage: we have ~4% of requests with chunked streaming stalls, 1.8% 5xxs in last 10m. top affected customers: cust-A, cust-D (high throughput).
alex (sre): hypothesis: prefetch + aggressive continuous batching at high QPS caused KV cache to be overwhelmed by unique keys, causing eviction cascade and backend I/O. That then increases per-token latency and microbatch completion waits.
sophia (eng-runtime): logs show a lot of "kv_fetch_latency_ms=2000+" traces around the time. also get this stack of backpressure logs:

```
cb-controller: queue_depth=1200 microbatch_wait_ms=3400 batch_size=64 kv_evictions=11234
worker-12: kv_fetch_latency_ms=2300 stall=true
```

maria (oncall): can we mitigate live without a full rollback? options: tighten max_batch_millis, disable prefetch, reduce kv_cache.max_items, temporarily route heavy customers to dedicated pool or smaller model.
alex (sre): low-risk hotfix: reduce continuous_batch.max_batch_millis from 30 -> 8 and set prefetch.enabled=false on cb-controller config. That should reduce batch accumulation and lessen unique KV pressure.
sophia (eng-runtime): agree. Also drop kv_cache.max_items by 25% to force less aggressive memory usage and avoid thrashing. We'll canary these changes to 2 nodes first.
maria (oncall): do it. I'm standing by to watch metrics. alex, can you run the change? I have the runbook open.
alex (sre): will push config via config-rollout script. command:

```
./config-rollout --env us-west-2 --service cb-controller --set continuous_batch.max_batch_millis=8 --set prefetch.enabled=false --set kv_cache.max_items=300000 --canary 2
```

starting canary now.
deploy-bot: config-rollout started: rollout_id=roll-1787654321-1 canary=2 target=cb-controller/us-west-2
sophia (eng-runtime): canary nodes up. streams show immediate drop in queue_depth on those two nodes from ~1200->300. kv_evictions trending down there.
ryan (product): any visible customer relief for cust-A? maria (oncall): cust-A traffic routed across cluster, but sampling shows their request p95 latency decreased from ~5.6s -> ~1.1s on the canary nodes. overall 5xxs decreased slightly.
alex (sre): after 2m of stable canary, proceeding to ramp. ramping now to 50%.
deploy-bot: rollout progress: 25% -> 50%
maria (oncall): metrics: 95th token latency for cluster dropping from 6.2s -> 2.0s as ramp continues. kv_evictions overall down 70%.
sophia (eng-runtime): still seeing a small number of stalled jobs where microbatch size spiked to 128; investigating whether any requests have pathological context/token patterns causing large KV key churn.
alex (sre): note: we reduced batch window which increases number of microbatches processed per second, but avoids huge single batch sizes which were thrashing the KV.
ryan (product): should we inform affected customers? short note saying we're mitigating a performance regression and monitoring.
maria (oncall): I'll draft a brief status update for CS to send to top affected customers: include ETA for full rollout and explanation.

maria (oncall): STATUS DRAFT: "We're aware of a regression in inference latency affecting streaming for a subset of requests. Our engineers identified a cache eviction cascade under high concurrency and have deployed a configuration mitigation (reduced batch window, disabled prefetch) which is significantly improving latency. We're monitoring and will follow up once fully rolled out."

ryan (product): good. mark major incident template and loop in account teams.
alex (sre): rollout at 90% now, metrics stay stable. I recommend leaving kv_cache.max_items decreased for 24h and then tune back with telemetry. We'll also add a short-term guard: kv_cache.eviction_rate_alert threshold tightened so we detect earlier.
sophia (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add smoother backoff on prefetch under high unique-key churn, and add a per-model prefetch cap. I'll open a ticket.
maria (oncall): will this breach SLA? current 5xx spike could have caused short blips but looks contained. ryan, product assess if compensatory credits needed.
ryan (product): will evaluate after full postmortem. tentatively no automated credits but we'll handle high-impact customers case-by-case.

alex (sre): final notes for handoff: 1) keep monitoring kv_evictions and 95pct token latency for us-west-2; 2) keep rollout at 100% for next 30m before revert of kv_cache.max_items; 3) if latency creeps back above 4s, revert continuous_batch.max_batch_millis to 30 and enable prefetch=false and scale up cb-controller by +2 nodes.
maria (oncall): I'm adding those into the oncall handoff checklist and tagging next oncall. Also saving the steps used and commands in the incident runbook thread.

incidents-bot: Incident acknowledged: incident_id=INC-1787 severity=P0 status=mitigated -> monitoring
maria (oncall): handing off to evening oncall @sophia (eng-runtime) will be the primary; archived logs and rollout_id saved. next_oncall, see pinned checklist: watch kv_evictions, p95 token latency, microbatch size distribution.
sophia (eng-runtime): ack handoff. I'll keep the config in place and start a follow-up issue for a controlled perf test to reproduce the cache blowup scenario.
alex (sre): leaving a note: run this query for quick snapshot:

```
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, avg(p95_token_latency) as p95, sum(kv_evictions) as evs FROM metrics WHERE region='us-west-2' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC;
```

maria (oncall): thanks team. closing pager; incident status = mitigated but monitoring for 2h. followup: postmortem assigned to sophia/alex, draft due EOD tomorrow.
